headline: Industrials Lead a Split Tape as Financials and Chips Sag
body_html:
Wall Street is trading unevenly at midday Friday, with more stocks rising than falling beneath a mixed surface. Of the 666 names we track, 395 are higher and 264 lower. These are intraday readings, and prices are not final.

Industrials are in front, up 0.9%, with consumer shares gaining 0.7% and energy up 0.34%. The standout is Modine Manufacturing, up 33.22%. Engineering firm Stantec has gained 13.17% and HVAC maker AAON 5.51%, so thermal and building-systems names are doing much of the lifting. On the other side, financials are down 1.94% and semiconductors 1.22%. AMD has dropped 4.45%.

Into the close, traders will watch the Middle East, where Hormuz and Bahrain headlines keep arriving even as oil heads for a second weekly decline. They will also watch the dollar, which sits near a 19-month high on bets that the Fed could raise rates. A late slide in financials or chips would change the tone of the session. The next trading day is Monday, November 16.

briefs.headline: Thermal and building-systems names surge
briefs.body: Modine Manufacturing is up 33.22% in midday trading, the biggest gain in our universe. Stantec has added 13.17% and AAON 5.51%. The cluster is pushing industrials to the top of the sector table at 0.9%, though all readings are intraday.

briefs.headline: Cerebras jumps while chip sector slips
briefs.body: Cerebras has surged about 13% after reporting stronger quarterly revenue and announcing a Microsoft deal. The wider semiconductor group is moving the other way, down 1.22%, and AMD has fallen 4.45%. The gains are narrow and the sector is under pressure.

briefs.headline: Financials are the session's weakest corner
briefs.body: Financials are down 1.94%, the steepest sector decline so far. Payments firm DLocal has lost 4.31%. Rate worries are in the background, with currency and bond markets pricing a firmer Fed, and the group's late-session direction will matter for the index.

briefs.headline: Oil heads for another weekly decline
briefs.body: Crude is set for a second straight weekly drop even as Washington keeps its blockade on Iran. The International Energy Agency says the world oil market is moving back toward surplus as Gulf exports recover. Energy shares are up 0.34% midday.

briefs.headline: Gulf tensions keep headlines coming
briefs.body: Iran says an LNG tanker struck a mine and exploded in the Strait of Hormuz. Its Revolutionary Guards also claim to have targeted a US early-warning radar in Bahrain. Separately, the UN nuclear watchdog says it is increasingly worried about an Iranian enrichment site.

briefs.headline: Dollar firm as yen tests key level
briefs.body: The dollar is hovering near a 19-month high as traders bet the Fed may raise rates, and the yen is testing the 160 level per dollar. The Indian rupee has weakened on higher oil and US yields. Currency moves are worth watching into the afternoon.
